page.title: Virtual event checklist for planners
page.description: A practical checklist covering registration, engagement, recording, follow‑up and asset timing for virtual events, with tool categories, timing rules and a comparison table for replay delivery.
page.h1: What belongs on a virtual event checklist?
page.definition: A virtual event checklist is a structured list of tasks, decisions and deliverables that ensures registration, engagement, recording, follow‑up and asset delivery are completed on time for online or hybrid gatherings. It also assigns owners, sets deadlines and flags late assets before they affect the live experience.
page.quick_answer: Create a master spreadsheet that lists every workstream, owner and due date. Lock registration, platform and speaker assets at least two weeks before the live date. West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations.

sections.h2: What registration steps belong on a virtual event checklist?

blocks.p: Registration steps cover platform set‑up, ticket types, confirmation flow and data capture. Build the registration page on the chosen platform, define free, paid and VIP tiers, configure automated confirmation and reminder emails, map fields to the CRM for lead routing, and test the full sign‑up flow on desktop and mobile.

ul: Choose event platform and enable registration page
Define ticket tiers such as free, paid, VIP
Configure automated confirmation and reminder emails
Map registration fields to CRM for lead routing
Test the end‑to‑end sign‑up flow on desktop and mobile

sections.h2: Which engagement tools should be planned for a virtual event?

blocks.p: Engagement tools include live chat, polls, Q&A, breakout rooms and gamified elements. Enable chat with assigned moderators, schedule polls at key agenda points, set up Q&A with up‑vote, create breakout sessions for networking, and add a leaderboard or badge system for participation.

ol: Enable live chat and assign moderators
Schedule polls at key agenda points
Set up Q&A with up‑vote feature
Add a leaderboard or badge system for participation

sections.h2: How do recording and replay delivery fit into the checklist?

blocks.p: Recording and replay delivery require capture settings, editing workflow and distribution timeline. Choose the capture method that matches the event type, allocate editing resources, and set a deadline for publishing the replay.

sections.h2: What follow‑up actions close the loop after a virtual event?

blocks.p: Follow‑up actions turn attendees into leads and feed the next campaign. Send the replay link within one to two days, push attendance data to the CRM for scoring, trigger a nurture sequence based on session topics, collect feedback through a short survey, and update the content library with edited clips.

ul: Send replay link within one to two days

sections.h2: When should assets be locked to avoid late delivery?

blocks.p: Asset lock dates protect the run of show from last‑minute changes. Finalize speaker slides, lower‑third graphics, video inserts and branding assets at least two weeks before the live date, and confirm the backup stream configuration during the technical check sixty minutes before go‑live.

faq.q: How far in advance should the run of show be finalized?
faq.a: Finalize the run of show at least two weeks before the live date, allowing time for speaker rehearsals, technical checks and backup stream configuration. This buffer also gives the production team space to adjust timing, insert lower‑third graphics and confirm platform settings.

faq.q: What is the minimum staffing needed for a simple webinar?
faq.a: A single producer can manage a basic webinar, handling platform controls, speaker cues and chat moderation, while a backup operator stands by for stream redundancy. If the agenda includes polls or breakout rooms, add a moderator to monitor interactions and a technical assistant for troubleshooting.

faq.q: Which tools help track checklist progress across teams?
faq.a: Project boards such as Asana, Monday.com or Airtable give each workstream a visible owner, due date and status, while a shared calendar keeps rehearsal slots and go‑live times aligned. Integrate the board with a CRM like HubSpot so attendance data flows automatically into lead scoring.

faq.q: When should the replay be sent to attendees?
faq.a: Send the replay within one to two days after the event while the content is fresh, and include a short highlight reel for quick consumption. Add a call‑to‑action linking to the next webinar or a downloadable resource to keep momentum.
